To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The use of antibiotics for the treatment of bovine mastitis can lead to antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic residues in milk, which are harmful to human health.”
(1) The use of a combination of two antibiotics in the diluents used to extend bull semen is an effective means of preventing bacterial contamination of semen.
the use of antibiotics to control bacteria contamination of bull semen can lead to yeast contamination of the semen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the effect of the addition of a number of antibiotics to bull semen.
the study of the effect of the addition of antibiotics on bacterial and yeast contamination of bovine semen.
the isolation of yeasts from 498 samples of bovine semen treated with antibiotics and the identification of these organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of bacteria in bull semen is of no significance to the fertility of the semen.
the yeast flora of bovine spermatozoa is a reflection of the flora of the genital tract of the bull and that it is not a specific flora.
the presence of yeast in semen is not an indication of contamination by bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the yeast contamination in bull semen was mainly caused by the contamination of the seminal vesicles and the epididymis.

, the antibiotics, sulfonamide, tetracycline and penicillin were not effective for the prevention of the contamination of diluted bull semen with yeasts, but that, streptomycin and chloramphenicol, which are known as the antibiotics for the treatment of Candida infection in the human being, were effective.
the yeast contamination of diluted bull semen was not a major problem in our country, although the yeasts were found to be a cause of chronic endometritis in two bulls.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a yeast extract in a yeast extract-glucose medium (YEGM) is a good alternative to the use of peptone in the yeast extract-malt extract-glucose medium for yeast isolation from clinical specimens.
the yeast species Candida albicans and Candida glabrata are the most commonly isolated yeast species from the vagina.
it is possible to develop a yeast strain for use in the production of biofuels.
